review.recommendation: Preserve PR ref/audit as an incomplete prototype; do not compile-import 42bd7712. evidence: harw-cli/src/n8n_bridge.rs begins: Library-level n8n outbound bridge. No inbound listener or TUI wiring. Full-tree grep finds N8nBridge::new only in unit tests; no production ReqwestN8nTransport::new or resolve_n8n_credential caller. [n8n] only parsed/validated, never consumed by a session. Therefore importing this does not provide advertised TUI bridge behavior.

n8n_credentials.rs profile_root reads HARW_HOME or HOME/.harw, ignoring active profile and --home resolution. It claims profile-relative storage but actually resolves credentials/n8n at home root. MCP preset separately embeds file:~/.harw/credentials/n8n/default.token despite telling user to use profile credentials.

Credential ownership derives UID from /proc/self, defaulting to u32::MAX on failure; ordinary macOS credentials fail. Unconditional std::os::unix imports also lack cross-platform gating. It uses symlink_metadata followed by separate read_to_string rather than current secure-open/secret-store path.

n8n_wire.rs creates independent reqwest::blocking::Client with HTTPS/timeout only: no Harw egress resolver/policy, no explicit redirect or proxy policy, and unbounded response.bytes(). n8n_bridge.rs blocks thread during retries and has no job cancellation wiring.

Useful prototype pieces exist: envelope correlation, event IDs, retry classification, process-local dedupe, disabled default, restricted config merging, workflow template. These do not establish a usable end-to-end integration.
Only user-visible entrypoint changes are MCP setup/check n8n with a placeholder URL, separate from webhook event transport. New endpoint preset alone is not a working event bridge.
